items.title: Gaza City, Palestinian Territories, Palestinian Territories: Egypt, Jordan, the UAE, Qatar, Indonesia, Saudi Arabia, Türkiye, and Pakistan jointly condemned Israel's rejection of the Trump Gaza plan.
items.description: Egypt, Jordan, the UAE, Qatar, Indonesia, Saudi Arabia, Türkiye, and Pakistan jointly condemned Israel's rejection of the Trump Gaza plan.
items.rawSummary: Gaza remains caught between a monitored disarmament-and-withdrawal framework, continued Israeli military activity and political pressure, and widening regional disagreement over the territory’s future.
items.analysis: The central ceasefire dispute remains whether Hamas disarmament and Israeli withdrawal proceed in parallel or whether withdrawal follows only after weapons are surrendered and verified. Peace Council Secretary General Nickolay Mladenov has described a phased mechanism involving mediators, U.S. personnel, and an international security force, while Israel would retain the ability to respond to imminent threats; the Council also says its funds are audited, do not pass through Hamas, and that violation monitoring is operating. Hamas has publicly backed an end to regional fighting and, in a meeting reported by Axios, reaffirmed a commitment to disarm and demilitarize Gaza, but this sits alongside the unresolved sequencing dispute and earlier indications that it was not prepared to disarm. Israeli-approved targeted strikes have continued, while National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir has advocated executions, expanded strikes, settlement in Gaza, and emigration, positions that conflict with the negotiated framework; regional governments have condemned Israel’s rejection of the plan, while Türkiye and the United States have publicly opposed displacement and the humanitarian and reconstruction crisis remains unresolved.

items.title: Mecca, Saudi Arabia: Trump provided additional commentary, stating the agreement shows the Middle East is coming together and represents a big, bold, and important first step for countries to defend themselves.
items.description: Trump provided additional commentary, stating the agreement shows the Middle East is coming together and represents a big, bold, and important first step for countries to defend themselves.
items.rawSummary: The Mecca Agreement, a mutual-defense pact between Saudi Arabia, Pakistan, and Turkey, has been formally signed and endorsed by its signatories and the United States, establishing a new regional security framework with potential for expansion.
items.analysis: The Mecca Agreement has solidified into a formal mutual-defense pact among Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan, with Turkish President Erdoğan explicitly comparing its collective security commitment to NATO's Article 5. This framework, which permits future membership and has seen Egypt mentioned as a potential candidate, represents a significant consolidation of geopolitical alignment among major non-Western states. U.S. President Trump has provided a strong public endorsement, framing the pact as a bold and positive development for regional self-defense, thereby adding significant international backing to the alliance's perception and potential influence.

items.title: Riyadh, Saudi Arabia: Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan said the Mecca Agreement among Saudi Arabia, Türkiye and Pakistan could be opened to other countries, including Egypt.
items.description: Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan said the Mecca Agreement among Saudi Arabia, Türkiye and Pakistan could be opened to other countries, including Egypt.
items.rawSummary: Saudi Arabia is balancing continued reliance on U.S. security support with broader regional diplomacy and gradual domestic curriculum changes under Vision 2030.
items.analysis: Saudi Arabia and other Gulf states remain dependent on U.S. security support while reported frustration with Washington’s handling of the Iran war is encouraging discussion of broader regional defense partnerships. That regional recalibration is also reflected in Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan’s statement that the Mecca Agreement among Saudi Arabia, Türkiye and Pakistan could be opened to other countries, including Egypt. Separately, Saudi Arabia has continued moderating school curricula under Vision 2030, including changes to references to Jerusalem and Israel. These developments point to a combination of strategic diversification and domestic policy repositioning, though they do not by themselves establish a formal change in Saudi security alignment.

items.description: A Khartoum military parade displayed new Iranian 107mm and 122mm rocket launchers, artillery, and Pakistani-made Muhafiz armored vehicles.
items.rawSummary: Foreign military support for Sudan's armed forces continues through arms displays and diplomatic backing, with recent drone combat highlighting the involvement of multiple international backers in the conflict.
items.analysis: A military parade in Khartoum showcased new Iranian and Pakistani-made weapons, including rocket launchers and armored vehicles, indicating sustained external military support amid the ongoing conflict. Turkish President Erdogan's statement of continued support adds a diplomatic dimension to this internationalized aspect of the war. The recent incident where the Sudan Army's AKINCI drone reportedly shot down a Chinese-made CH-95 drone operated by the UAE-backed RSF in an air-to-air engagement further underscores the diverse foreign weaponry and backers involved, escalating the conflict's technological and proxy dimensions.

items.title: Parchin Military Complex, near Tehran, Iran: Iran’s judiciary chief Mohseni-Ejei announced that upcoming appointments will include reshuffles based partly on recommendations from the IRGC and Ministry of Intelligence.
items.description: Iran’s judiciary chief Mohseni-Ejei announced that upcoming appointments will include reshuffles based partly on recommendations from the IRGC and Ministry of Intelligence.
items.rawSummary: Iranian officials are asserting victory and preparing for potential conflict amid stalled U.S. diplomatic talks and economic pressures, while a new incident barring French diplomats from Tehran has added to regional tensions.
items.analysis: Senior Iranian officials continue to declare victory in the recent conflict and prepare for expanded operations, despite growing economic strain from halted oil exports and disrupted imports. Intelligence indicates Tehran has used the post-agreement period to rebuild military capabilities and coordinate regional militias, with hard-line factions consolidating control over military, internal security, and judicial structures, as evidenced by the judiciary chief's announcement of reshuffles based on IRGC and intelligence recommendations. Diplomatic talks with the United States remain stalled, with the Foreign Ministry citing U.S. violations of the June memorandum of understanding as the reason negotiations have not begun. Iran is simultaneously pursuing alternative regional engagements, such as maritime transit negotiations with Oman, addressing the status of pilots in Qatar through Red Cross correspondence, and advocating for a sovereignty-protecting mechanism for commercial shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. In the latest development, Iran has barred two French diplomats from returning to their posts in Tehran, accused by Iran of participating in anti-regime protests, which further strains diplomatic relations.
